reader.requirement: At --std 85 the SYNCHRONIZED clause (SYNC/SYNCHRONIZED, optionally LEFT or RIGHT) is the means of synchronizing an elementary item, with its effect on alignment, implicit FILLER and external format specified by the implementor (VI.5.13.4 GR8), its PICTURE/USAGE/SIGN size governing truncation (GR5), and its syntax limits enforced (elementary only, not USAGE INDEX); the witness covers SYNC/SYNC LEFT/SYNCHRONIZED RIGHT on COMP items only.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel >= 2023 / ConstructRegistry.Check(SyncOnGroup2023): SYNC on a group item refused below 2023 (COBOL0900), admitted at 2023
dialectLevel < 2002 && Usage.Index: SYNC on a USAGE INDEX item refused at 85 (COBOL2405, §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR6), admitted 2002+

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: SYNC on a group item is refused at 85 and admitted at 2023; SYNC on a USAGE INDEX item is refused at 85 and admitted 2002+; the layout (no alignment, no implicit FILLER) is the same at every edition.

reader.notes: The clause is parsed and recorded (DataBinder.BindEntry -> DataItem.Synchronized) and the layout never reads it (BitLayout/RecordLayout carry no Synchronized reference), which is the implementor determination DOC-A.1-195 publishes: a one-character natural boundary, no alignment, no implicit FILLER. The 1985 syntax limits are enforced on their own arms (group refused below 2023, USAGE INDEX refused below 2002). DOC-A.1-195 cites only §2023 clauses; the 1985 obligation it discharges is §1985:VI.5.13.4 GR8.
